rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-6 - own field evaluations of basin irrigation events at Pingluo (inflow, advance/recession, infiltrometer tests, soil survey) and own runs of SRFR/SIRMOD and ISAREG. Q2: Section 4.2 and Eqs. 3-9 - ISAREG uses FAO56 ETc and the Stewart yield-ET relation combined with the Ayers-Westcot salinity equation to compute ETc adj; Section 6.2 and Tables 11-12 - improved schedules searched interactively with ISAREG and SRFR for non-saline and saline soils, giving season water savings of 21-30% with zero percolation (Table 11) and 8-22% with leaching fractions on saline soils (Table 12); Section 5.2 - ISAREG present-condition values stated to be similar to those observed in field evaluations, and Fig. 4 - SRFR calibrated on observed advance/recession. Q4: Tables 8, 11, 12 and Section 4.2 - model computes percolation, capillary rise, available soil water, ETc adj and salinity-corrected TAW and depletion fraction, i.e. the intermediate variables through which scheduling controls percolation, salinity and yield. Q5: Tables 8, 11, 12 - results reported separately for wheat, maize and wheat-maize intercrop (plus three TAW soil classes and two salinity levels). Q7: Section 6.2 last paragraph and Conclusions - savings achievable only under condition that upstream diversions are reduced so drainage functions, the drainage system is upgraded to lower the water table, precision zero leveling and higher inflow rates are adopted, and delivery scheduling is adapted; farmers alone cannot implement without support. Q8: Section 5.2 - some uncertainty remains in the ISAREG simulations of capillary rise and percolation; Section 4.2 - a mechanistic model would be required to properly simulate salt dynamics, the salinity subroutine is a simplification and Eqs. 6-9 are valid only when relative yield loss does not exceed 50%; root depth and GWD scenarios assumed.
rows.notes: The claim is methodological (study used Eq. 3 within a FAO56-based simulation model to search improved schedules under salinity and water scarcity), which the study does. Doubt on Q2: the improved-schedule scenarios (Tables 11-12) are model outputs not checked against measurements; validation is only for present conditions (ISAREG present scenario vs field evaluations; SRFR inverse solution vs observed advance/recession). Q3 no: improved schedules rest on simulation alone. Q6 no: results at field/basin scale (e.g. basin B1); district-scale use is only recommended. Q9 no: ranges/S.D. are given only for field geometry (Table 3) and present performance (Table 7), not for the simulated savings or salinity results.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a combined field-evaluation and modeling study in the Huinong Irrigation District, Ningxia, single district, 1999 weather data.
